National institutions and partners have strengthened capacities to manage food and nutrition programmes and social protection systems
Food Systems Transition Pathway•Convergence of Agendas (food systems and climate change)•Food Systems Roadmap
WFP/UNIDO CAMFORT (Cameroon Food Optimization, Resilience and Technology) project launch
South-South Cooperation exchange visits: HGSF, value chain development
WFP/ARC (African Risk Capacity) scoping mission to assess impact of climate-related risks on food systems
Joint proposal on blended financing mechanisms to support micro-credits to SHF (SHECAN initiative)
Drone training on disaster mapping, search and rescue for MINAT staff
INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY
STRENGTHENING
Social Protection System• Institutionalization workshop for sustainability of the Social
Safety Nets Project (Projet Filets Sociaux - PFS)• Training in cash programming for MINAS and MINAT
personnel• MOU with MINAS anchored on learning opportunities,
improving accountability to affected people and enhancing social protection coverage
Early Warning System (EWS) capacity assessment• MOU between Stakeholders to operationalize EWS
Food security assessments• Food Safety Management System (FSMS) survey• National Food Security and Nutrition Assessment (ENSAN)• Food prices monitoring• Cadre Harmonisé analyses

The government and partners can reach vulnerable populations and respond to emergencies throughout the year
Global Commodity Management Facility (GCMF)•Extended support to Sudan and Nigeria (including Cameroon, Chad and CAR) through the Douala Corridor
48,350 mt of food dispatched to Chad to support the Sudanese crisis response
119,700 mt of food received 99,000 mt dispatched through the Douala Corridor
Support to MINSANTE•490,100 mosquito nets transported to 99 health centres in Northwest and Southwest regions•393 cubic metres of vaccines (6.7 million doses) transported•257 officials trained in thermo-sensitive logistics and Quality Management Systems
SERVICE PROVISION
UN Humanitarian Air Service• 3 destinations: Yaounde, Maroua, N’Djamena (Chad)• 150 flights• 3,175 passengers and 12 mt of light cargo transported• 53 humanitarian organisations served• 98% passenger satisfaction rate• Regional training on dangerous goods led by HQ
Local Procurement• 4,013 mt of locally produced sorghum and salt • 3,000 mt of imported rice• USD 4.9 million injected into the local economy

CROSS-CUTTING RESULTS
1. Improved gender equality and women’s empowerment 2. Affected people are treated in a manner that ensures and promotes their safety, dignity and integrity and hold WFP and partners accountable
Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment
•Participation in the 68th Commission on the Status of Women (CSW68) led by MINPROFF
•MoU and action plan with MINPROFF drafted
•MoU with UNFPA for joint programming and advocacy
•Implementation of 2-Yyear women’s empowerment project with UNWOMEN in Far North
•Supported MINEDUB and MINPROFF participation in the 1st Pan African Conference in Girls and Women’s Education.
•Award programme for best performing teenage girls in the Southwest Region under the Education Cannot Wait coalition
•11,200 women participated in PULCCA activities, capacity strengthening and establishing IGAs, VSLAs
•60 percent of WFP beneficiaries were women
Gender-Based Violence (GBV)•Developed training modules for staff and cooperating partners•Advocacy and information sessions during the 16 days of activism against GBV
Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA)• Trained 150 staff from 21 cooperating partners and
stakeholders on PSEA
Accountability to Affected People (AAP)• National AAP Working Group lead• WFP led the rollout of the joint Humanitarian Community
Feedback Mechanism (HCFM)• 100% compliance with the 6 assurance CFM standards• 7 feedback channels: hotline, complaints committees,
suggestion boxes, helpdesks, focus group discussions, cooperating partners and WFP staff• Community Engagement Action Plan (CE-AP) developed• Piloted BHA project: ‘Understand, Engage and Respond:
Inclusive tool for Inclusive systems’• Assisted people reported improved access, safety and
dignity in WFP programmes compared to early 2024

Partnerships
Collaboration with the Government•Lead role in disaster preparedness, mitigation and anticipatory actions under MINAT•Implementation of PULCCA•Tripartite agreement between the Government and African Development Bank (AfDB) for flood response•Ongoing discussions with the Government and Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) to support school feeding
Private Sector partnerships• Cargill project implementation in the NWSW• Partnership with ZEP-RE for innovative agricultural risk
management solutions• Discussions with JICA on rive value chain development
Localization• 38 field-level agreements (FLAs) with 22 NGOs (73% local)
for activities implementation
UN inter-agency collaboration• Joint initiative with UNIDO (CAMFORT project) on food
systems approach for small and medium-sized enterprises• Joint HCFM• Several MoUs and LoUs: UNFPA, UNOPS
PARTNERSHIPS AND FINANCIAL
OVERVIEW
Financial Overview
Available resources in 2024: 76% of needs-based plan
Cameroon Government contribution: USD 44.8 million
